title: Why Meetings Spend Hours on Fonts and Minutes on Strategy
alt_title_1: Parkinson's 1957 Law of Triviality: The Bike-Shed Trap
alt_title_2: Stop Spending 3 Weeks on Logos and 10 Minutes on Revenue
description_hook: In his 1957 book Parkinson's Law, C. Northcote Parkinson formulated the Law of Triviality: a committee approves a 10-million-pound reactor in 2.5 minutes, then argues 45 minutes over a cheap bike shed. Here is how to stop personal bikeshedding.

scenes.headline: 2 Minutes on a Reactor, 45 on a Bike Shed
scenes.stat_label: TIME SPENT GROWS INVERSELY TO FINANCIAL STAKES
bullets: 350-pound staff bike shed debated for 45 minutes
scenes.narration: Why does a committee approve a ten-million-pound nuclear reactor in two minutes, then argue for forty-five minutes over a bike shed?

scenes.headline: Parkinson's 1957 Law of Triviality
scenes.stat_label: EASY OPINIONS CROWD OUT HARD THINKING
bullets: Reactor math feels too complex to critique safely
Everyone understands roof tiles and coffee budgets
scenes.narration: Historian C. Northcote Parkinson explained this in 1957 as the Law of Triviality: complex, high-stakes math intimidates people into silence, whereas everyone understands roof shingles and coffee budgets enough to debate endlessly.
scenes.source: C. Northcote Parkinson, 'High Finance, or the Point of Vanishing Interest' (1957)

scenes.headline: Personal Bikeshedding Disguises Procrastination
scenes.left_body: 3 weeks tweaking Notion icons, hex codes & logos -> $0 shipped
scenes.right_body: 90% of deep hours on product value, distribution & cashflow math
scenes.narration: Solo builders fall into personal bikeshedding constantly: spending three weeks tweaking Notion icons, color palettes, and logos while spending ten minutes on distribution or revenue.

scenes.headline: Cap Cosmetics at 15 Minutes; Fund the Reactor
scenes.stat_label: PROTECTING HIGH-LEVERAGE HOURS COMPOUNDS REAL ASSETS
scenes.stat_subtext: 15-min timer on styling • 90-min morning block on core asset
scenes.narration: Cap every cosmetic bike-shed decision at fifteen minutes on a timer, and force ninety percent of your morning energy onto the core reactor.

scenes.headline: Starve Trivial Polish of Your Prime Hours
scenes.stat_label: PUT YOUR BEST BRAIN CELLS ON THE BIGGEST LEVER
bullets: Use default templates for every reversible detail
Spend prime morning energy only on asymmetric math
scenes.narration: Starve trivial polish of oxygen so your sharpest hours compound the big levers that actually pay.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on C. Northcote Parkinson (1957)
